$doc: Map pool. Each entry binds an art pack to generation + enemy overrides. Adding a map = add an art pack under art/packs/<id>/ and one entry here. No logic changes.

mansion.$note: Ambient is deliberately low but above graphics.json -> minAmbientFloor: the manor lights itself with candles, a fire in most rooms and moonlight through the windows, and the fog does the rest.

viscera.$note: Ambient is a hair warmer and lower than the manor's: almost everything you navigate by inside the beast is emissive - bile, nerve cord, spore blooms, eyes - and a cool ambient fill was washing that out. The fog is the colour of old blood, which is what closes the far wall of a big chamber.

abyss.$note: Ambient is cold blue and a shade higher than the other two maps: half of what you navigate by here is a lit tank or a viewing pane, and those are emissive rather than lit, so the fill is only doing the corners. The fog is near-black with a blue cast, which is what makes a sixteen-metre hall close down at the far end and what makes the water behind the glass read as depth rather than as a painted wall.

crypt.$note: Ambient is COLD and the practicals are all flame, which is the split the art guide asks for and the thing this map got wrong first: a warm ambient (#2c2a33) on top of a hundred candle niches made every room the same shade of orange, with no temperature anywhere for the warmth to be warm against. Cold blue-grey fill, warm tallow and oil, and the Rot's violet reading as a third thing that is neither. The fog is a warm near-black - grave dust rather than sea water - which is what makes a twenty-four metre column hall close down at the far end and what keeps the one gilded sarcophagus in the map reading as gold rather than as a lamp.

forge.$note: The temperature split here is INVERTED from the other maps and the ambient is what makes it work. The facility lights itself cold - arc white and cyan, red where a circuit failed - and the only warm light anywhere is the mountain leaking in, so the fill has to be cold too or the Works stops reading as a different place from the Mountain and the whole map goes one colour. The fog is a warm near-black: ash and sulphur rather than sea water, which is what closes down a sixteen-metre caldera at the far end and what keeps a lava lake reading as a surface rather than as a lamp. Ambient is a shade lower than abyss because half of what you navigate by here is emissive - the heat register round every wall, the crack network in a hot floor, a rack of status lights - and the fill is only doing the corners.

heartwood.$note: Ambient is COLD and slightly green - the fill is what a forest night looks like through a hole in a trunk - and every practical in the Bower half is warm sap, wax or ember against it. That split is the only thing that makes a moth lantern read as a moth lantern; a green ambient under green foxfire would flatten the Thicket half into one wash and take the wood colour out of the whole map. The fog is a warm near-black: leaf mould and dust rather than sea water, which is what closes a twenty-four metre bark canyon down at the far end and what keeps a sap well reading as a surface rather than as a lamp. Intensity sits between the manor and the abyss because a good half of what you navigate by here is emissive - the register round every wall, a bank of gills, a comb full of lit honey - and the fill is only doing the corners.

prison.$note: Ambient is COLD and the practicals split by wing, which is the whole reason the two halves of this building read as two buildings. The Blocks light themselves with a forty-watt tungsten night circuit - amber, sagging, never switched off - and the Ward with failing fluorescent and x-ray boxes, a green-white that is colder than the fill itself. A warm ambient would take the tungsten's job away and leave the map one colour, which is the finding this project has now paid for twice (docs/art/ROOM_REVIEW.md). The fog is a warm near-black: coal smoke and carbolic rather than sea water, and it is what closes a twenty-four metre landing down at the far end and what keeps a barred window reading as a picture rather than as a lamp. Intensity sits with the manor's, because a good half of what a player navigates by here is the emissive night course along every wall and the fill is only doing the corners.
